CASE001.title: Beijing: misleading mobile-data plan pricing
CASE001.case_text: Zhongzhi Wireless advertised a large mobile-data allowance for CNY 9 per month, but the actual offer did not match the advertisement.

CASE002.title: Hangzhou: cosmetic advertised as treating skin conditions
CASE002.case_text: Hangzhou Xunyou Trading promoted a cosmetic during livestream sales as treating redness, itching, stinging and acne, potentially confusing cosmetics with medicines.

CASE003.title: Guangzhou: ordinary food promoted as a treatment
CASE003.case_text: Guangzhou Qihuang Yidao Culture Media claimed ordinary food could treat disc herniation, joint pain and constipation, potentially confusing food with medicine.

CASE004.title: Beijing: fabricated weight-loss testimonials
CASE004.case_text: Beijing Xuanyantang Biotechnology purchased livestream support services and used false comments claiming that two boxes of ordinary jelly food could cause weight loss of 3.5 or 10 kilograms.

CASE005.title: Hangzhou: unsupported beauty-device performance
CASE005.case_text: Hangzhou Jiefu Culture Media claimed a beauty device prevented rebound and equated one minute of use with over one hundred thousand abdominal crunches, without supporting evidence.

CASE006.title: Qingdao: treatment claims for an ordinary ointment
CASE006.case_text: Qingdao Kemanchi Trading promoted an ordinary ointment that was neither a medicine nor a medical device, using a fabricated story of a user regaining mobility to imply treatment effects.

CASE007.title: Guangzhou: exaggerated functions in livestream sales
CASE007.case_text: Livestream sellers for Guangzhou Chuangfan Supin Technology invented or exaggerated the functions of cosmetics, home appliances and coffee beverage powders beyond supplied product information.

CASE008.title: Guangzhou: invented or exaggerated product performance
CASE008.case_text: Livestream promotion by Guangzhou Xinxuan Network Information Technology exaggerated or invented the functions of yeast-formulated milk powder, foods and mugwort patches.

CASE009.title: Zhuji: imitation pearls sold as genuine
CASE009.case_text: A livestream seller sold imitation pearls and necklaces as genuine pearls and used forged authentication certificates.

CASE010.title: Hotan: staged jade-discovery livestream
CASE010.case_text: Hotan Shengxian Jewelry buried jade in advance and staged an excavation, telling viewers the jade had just been found on site.

CASE011.title: Hong Kong Baihong: misleading food-category claims
CASE011.case_text: Online advertisements for ordinary food used wording that could lead consumers to mistake it for a health food product.

CASE012.title: Qiandaohu Chunxin: false royal-jelly claims
CASE012.case_text: Website promotion for royal jelly included false pharmacological effects, user feedback and cooperating testing institutions, and used medical terminology in ordinary-food advertising.

CASE013.title: Henan Weimengdi: absolute claims for a spot-removal product
CASE013.case_text: Advertisements used absolute expressions such as the world's most stable, safest, most scientific and most thorough.

CASE014.title: Yunnan Xinghao: disease claims for camel milk powder
CASE014.case_text: Advertisements claimed camel milk powder could lower blood sugar and regulate high blood pressure, blood sugar and blood lipids, presenting ordinary food as preventing or treating disease.

CASE015.title: Wuxi Lilu: influencer endorsement of health food
CASE015.case_text: Health-food advertisements that had not undergone advertising review used an online influencer's name and image to recommend and endorse the product.

CASE016.title: Chengmai Hengsheng Hospital: health claims for beverage powder
CASE016.case_text: Advertisements for an ordinary beverage powder claimed liver protection, detoxification and regulation of high blood pressure, blood sugar and blood lipids, linking it to treatment and health functions.

CASE017.title: Yuanjian Henghui: disease claims for ordinary food
CASE017.case_text: Advertisements claimed ordinary food could remove kidney stones, relieve gout, dissolve blood clots, clear blood vessels and prevent dementia.

CASE018.title: Weifang Huahong: medical language in tea advertising
CASE018.case_text: Advertisements for ordinary tea referred to lung nodules, pharyngitis and throat pain or swelling, potentially confusing it with medicines or medical devices.

CASE019.title: Shanghai Gaoyijiang: health claims for bottled water
CASE019.case_text: Advertisements for ordinary bottled water claimed sustained and powerful antioxidant effects and protection against free radicals.

CASE020.title: Shanghai Shanxixi: disease claims for beverage powder
CASE020.case_text: Advertisements claimed an ordinary beverage powder could address rhinitis, allergies, asthma, lung nodules and constipation, and improve immunity.

CASE021.title: Beijing Qingtian Shukang: treatment and immunity claims
CASE021.case_text: An ordinary beverage powder sold through a proprietary mini-program was promoted as improving gastrointestinal function and immunity and preventing or treating diarrhea and allergies.

CASE022.title: Beijing Meiye: unsupported beauty claims for drinks
CASE022.case_text: An online shop promoted ordinary drinks with unsubstantiated claims of skin whitening, spot reduction, brighter and firmer skin, and melanin inhibition.

CASE023.title: Beijing Dangdang: false dietary-fibre claim
CASE023.case_text: An online shop advertised brown rice as rich in dietary fibre although its content did not meet the applicable food-standard conditions for that claim.

CASE024.title: Beijing Nuoshi: health claims and unverified testimonials
CASE024.case_text: A WeChat account promoted ordinary foods as improving immunity, protecting the liver, relieving symptoms and slowing ageing, and used unverifiable user reviews.

CASE025.title: Shanwei: cognitive and sleep claims for candy
CASE025.case_text: A Taobao shop advertised ordinary pressed candy as reducing anxiety and stress, enhancing memory and improving sleep.

CASE026.title: Shanwei Red Bay: health claims for a peptide drink
CASE026.case_text: A Pinduoduo shop advertised an ordinary bovine-spleen peptide drink as nourishing the spleen and stomach and regulating or restoring immunity.

CASE027.title: Hubei: disease claims for deer-antler foods
CASE027.case_text: A WeChat account promoted deer-antler blood and foods as lowering blood pressure, relieving rheumatism and enhancing immunity, linking them to various diseases and symptoms.

CASE028.title: Fangxian: unsupported whitening claim for hand wash
CASE028.case_text: An e-commerce seller advertised skin-whitening effects for a hand wash registered as an ordinary cosmetic.

CASE029.title: Zhongshan: unsupported cookware materials and savings
CASE029.case_text: A cookware company claimed to use aerospace-grade materials and steel meeting surgical-scalpel standards, and published unverifiable annual oil and electricity savings.

CASE030.title: Zhongshan: cosmetic effects absent from product filings
CASE030.case_text: A Douyin shop advertised soothing ingredients in a facial cleanser and nourishing effects in a cream, although those effects were absent from the product filing information.
